prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but the “best” pick depends on your dates, budget, kids’ ages and whether you’ll have a car. A few quick questions first will let me give specific listings:
- When are you traveling and how many nights?
- What’s your budget per night (or total)?
- Any must-have amenities (parking, crib, fenced yard, washer/dryer, elevator)?
- Do you want to be walkable to restaurants/parks or prefer quiet/suburban?

While you answer, here are immediate recommendations and practical tips for a family of four visiting Nashville.

Best neighborhoods for families
- 12South — very walkable, family-friendly restaurants, playgrounds; charming bungalows and small houses.
- Germantown — close to downtown, quieter, parks, good restaurants; newer condos and renovated rowhouses.
- East Nashville — quirky, local vibe, parks and kid‑friendly cafes; lots of whole-house rentals.
- Hillsboro Village / Belmont — near the zoo, Vanderbilt and green spaces; good for younger kids.
- Green Hills — suburban feel, shopping, quieter streets; larger homes if you want space.
- The Gulch / Downtown — very convenient for attractions but noisier and more expensive.

Type of rental to prioritize
- Entire home or townhouse with 2+ bedrooms (space and privacy).
- Ground-floor or a single-story bungalow if stairs are a concern.
- Washer/dryer, full kitchen, safe layout for kids, and outdoor space if possible.
- On‑site or free off‑street parking if you’ll rent a car.

Key filters and search strategy (Airbnb/other platforms)
- Set property type to “Entire place” and beds to at least 2.
- Use “Family/kid friendly,” check for “crib” or “pack‑and‑play” and “high chair.”
- Filter for “Free parking on premises” and “Washer.”
- Prefer “Superhost” and sort by review score; read recent reviews for family-specific feedback.
- Check cancellation policy and house rules (noise/parties).
- Look for “self check‑in” if arriving late.

Amenity checklist for families
- 2+ bedrooms, 1+ bath per 3–4 people ideal
- Crib/pack-and-play and high chair (or ask host)
- Washer/dryer and full kitchen
- Air conditioning, blackout curtains for naps
- Secure/fenced yard or safe outdoor play area
- Off‑street parking or driveway
- Safe stairs or single story if little kids
- First-aid basics and baby-proofing (if needed; confirm with host)

Budget and timing
- Typical nightly rates vary widely: off-season 120–220 midrange, high season and weekends 250–500+ for central or premium homes. Major events (CMA Fest, big concerts) spike prices — book early.

Red flags to avoid
- Lots of noise complaints in recent reviews
- Listings with very few reviews or pictures
- Hosts who refuse to confirm baby gear availability
- Strict house rules about kids/guests or party-friendly neighborhoods

If you want, tell me your dates, budget and any must-have amenities and I’ll recommend specific types of listings or evaluate links you paste here.
